alec: FYI: after upgrading to py-sdk 0.9.x we started seeing huge latency spikes on our async embedding workers when concurrency >50. p99 from 200ms -> 1.2s.

rachel: ouch. any repro or recent changes you suspect?

alec: repro in a small app. We create one AsyncClient per worker task (bad pattern) but before 0.9.0 it didn't blow up. Now acquire time for connection climb and we see many short lived TCP connections. snippet: 
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key=API_KEY, max_connections=100, keepalive=True)
# but our worker code did `AsyncClient()` inside each request handler which spawns >100 tasks
```

jordan: creating client per request will defeat pooling. Did 0.9 change connector lifecycle so that TCP connections are not reused across clients? We changed how auth headers are attached (per-call vs per-client) which might force new transports.

alec: looks like the auth middleware now wraps the httpx client each call unless you pass auth=client.auth explicitly. That explains it. Our code path accidentally calls client.with_auth(token) in every task.

rachel: Can you try reusing one AsyncClient in a global lifetime (e.g., in FastAPI startup) and see if p99 improves?

alec: confirmed: switching to a single shared client (singleton) drops p99 back to ~220ms. But still not ideal. Also observed a small fd leak on long runs: fd count increases slowly.

jordan: fd leak could be due to session objects not being closed when client is GC'd. We have typing stubs for AsyncClient but they don't advertise __aenter__/__aexit__ properly which leads folks to not use `async with`. We should: 1) fix the typing to make misuse obvious, 2) ensure client.__del__ logs a warning and calls aclose() if loop running, 3) add explicit telemetry for pool stats.

infra-bot: diag job scheduled: /infra/diag/connpool/1799951234 run at 2026-12-03T09:12:00Z. Collecting netstat, fd counts, httpx transport stats.

alec: another oddity: retry behavior changed. Before, transient 5xx triggered quick backoff. Now we sometimes get 429s and client retries aggressively, making more connections. Can we get better default retry/backoff for streaming/embeddings?

jordan: Noted. We'll add separate retry profile for low-latency workloads: fewer retries, jitter, and circuit-breaker threshold. Also expose an opt-in parameter `retry_profile="low_latency"`.

rachel: Feature request: expose live pool metrics -> {in_use, available, total, waiters} and a sync/async API `await client.metrics()` so infra teams can alert on high waiters.

jordan: good idea. I'll add low-effort HTTP endpoint on the client and wire it into Console metrics. PR planned.

docbot: doc note: add example for FastAPI showing client as a startup singleton and recommended max_connections for embeddings vs chat.

alec: short-term mitigations for anyone hitting this: 1) reuse a single AsyncClient per process 2) set max_connections to a conservative value (32) 3) avoid creating per-call auth wrappers 4) pin to 0.9.1-nightly once fix lands.

jordan: action items: open PR to fix typing + add metrics endpoint + adjust default retry profile. I'll include a unit test that asserts no fd leak when creating and closing many clients.

infra-bot: ticket created: RDW-4678 connpool/retry regression (assigned jordan).

alec: thanks team, will monitor after PR and switch to singleton in our workers now :thumbsup:
